diagnostic_evidence.quote: when $\omega > 1$ is used (which is the case of interest in overrelaxation) it cannot be guaranteed that positive definite matrices are generated.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated input domain allows iterations that immediately leave the PD or invertible domain. For example, with $m=n=k=1$, $A_1=1$, $X_0=2$, $Y_0=1$, and $\omega=2$, PD-OR gives $S_1(Y_0)=1$ and $X_1=0$, so its requested Cholesky factor and next inverse do not exist. Likewise, Cholesky-OR with $L_0=2$, $R_0=1$, and $\omega=2$ gives $L_1=0$. Thus both affine schemes lack a domain-preservation condition on their advertised inputs.

failure_location.quote: Matrix collection $\bA$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{assumption 1},  initial matrices $(X_0, Y_0) \in \caC_m \times \caC_n$, and relaxation parameter $\omega >0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the algorithmic inputs to a domain known to keep every affine update PD or invertible, such as the sufficiently local regime used by the local theorem, or add an explicit admissibility check and conditional termination. For a global unconditional PD guarantee, PD-OR would need the underrelaxed range $0<\omega\leq1$; Cholesky-OR also needs canonical triangular positive-diagonal initial factors.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithms PD-OR and Cholesky-OR cannot be executed indefinitely for all inputs and all $\omega>0$ permitted by their algorithm blocks. The local convergence theorem is not invalidated because it separately requires initialization sufficiently close to a fixed point.
issues.title: Affine overrelaxation algorithms are not well-defined on their stated inputs
issues.why_classification: A complete repair requires materially narrowing the unrestricted input contract or adding a safeguarded procedure; merely editing an algebraic typo is insufficient. The paper's local guarantees can nevertheless be retained without new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking traces in the second frame condition gives $\sum_i\|\tilde x_i\|_2^2=n$, whereas the first condition gives $\sum_i\|\tilde x_i\|_2^2=k(n/k)^2=n^2/k$. These are incompatible unless $k=n$, contrary to the experiment's $k=55$, $n=50$. Moreover, the operator-scaling equations imply that $\tilde x_i=\sqrt n\,\ell_i R x_i$ has squared norm $n/k$ and sums to $I_n$; the stated choice $\alpha_i=n\ell_i^2$ does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first condition by $\|\tilde x_i\|_2^2=n/k$ and, with the stated convention $\tilde x_i=\alpha_iPx_i$, replace the correspondence by $P=R$ and $\alpha_i=\sqrt n\,\ell_i$.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the experimental instance cannot solve the defined frame-scaling problem, and the claimed equivalence between that problem and the operator-scaling instance is false.
issues.title: The stated frame-scaling problem is inconsistent and the scaling correspondence is wrong
issues.why_classification: The inconsistency is substantive, but the source supports a short algebraic repair that preserves the operator-scaling experiment and the intended frame-scaling interpretation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that the CP map $\Phi$ is positivity improving
A CP map $\Phi$ is said to be \emph{positivity improving} if it maps nonzero positive semidefinite (PSD) matrices to positive definite ones.

issues.failure_explanation: This frame CP map is not positivity improving when $n>1$: choose a nonzero vector $v$ orthogonal to $x_1$ and set $Z=vv^\top$. Then $Z$ is nonzero PSD but the first diagonal entry of $\Phi(Z)$ is $(x_1^\top v)^2=0$, so $\Phi(Z)$ is not positive definite. Consequently Theorem~\ref{thm: local convergence} does not apply to the reported frame experiment, regardless of whether its observed rates agree.

failure_location.quote: We see that the convergence rates of all three SOR methods are the same, validating the local convergence result in Theorem~\ref{thm: local convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “validating” by “consistent with” and explicitly note that this frame map is outside the positivity-improving regime, or prove a local convergence extension under weaker hypotheses that cover the frame instance.
issues.overall_effect: The experiment may provide evidence for a broader phenomenon, but it does not validate the stated theorem under that theorem's assumptions.
issues.title: The frame experiment lies outside the hypothesis of the theorem it is said to validate
issues.why_classification: A local qualification removes the unsupported validation claim without changing the theorem or experiment; extending the theorem would be nontrivial but is not necessary to repair the prose.
